risks.description: Section 2.4 commits Ledgerline to integrate 'any other systems as reasonably required by the Customer', while Section 6 excludes integrations other than NetSuite and Okta. This open-ended clause on a $48,000 fixed fee invites scope disputes and margin erosion.
risks.recommendation: Confirm in writing at kickoff that integrations are limited to NetSuite and Okta per Section 6, and route any other system requests through the Section 7 change order process.

source.quote: and any other systems as reasonably required by the Customer

risks.description: Go-live for three entities across two countries, with integration, PO matching and three payment rails, is targeted about 10 weeks after the effective date. The window includes US Thanksgiving and the Christmas/New Year holidays, and kickoff can slip to mid-November. Sequential dependencies (discovery, then 10 business days for data, then build, then 10 business days of UAT) leave almost no buffer.
risks.recommendation: Build a backward-scheduled plan at kickoff with holiday blackout dates, show the Customer the critical path, and agree a fallback such as phased go-live by entity if any dependency slips.

source.quote: go-live for all three entities on January 15, 2027

risks.description: Bank approval for ACH and virtual card has no due date, and bank onboarding often takes weeks. The Customer's bank setup for CAD EFT is not assigned to anyone. Either can block payments at go-live.
risks.recommendation: Ask the Customer at kickoff to start bank approvals immediately for ACH, virtual card and CAD EFT, set a due date in the project plan, and log a change order or phased payments go-live if approval is late.

source.quote: The Customer is responsible for obtaining its bank's approval to enable virtual card and ACH payments.

risks.description: 40% ($19,200) is payable on 'completion of UAT' and 30% ($14,400) on go-live, both controlled by the Customer. Section 3.2 says delays depend on the Customer but gives no remedy, timeline relief or fee for Customer-caused delay.
risks.recommendation: Agree at kickoff that UAT is complete when the 10-business-day UAT window closes or deemed acceptance applies, and that Customer-caused delays trigger a change order under Section 7. Document every late dependency in status reports.

source.quote: 40% on completion of UAT, 30% on go-live

risks.description: Deemed acceptance applies 5 business days after delivery, but the Customer has 10 business days to complete UAT. 'Material defect' is not defined. The mismatch will cause disputes over when deliverables, and the UAT payment, are accepted.
risks.recommendation: Agree at kickoff which period governs the configured Platform (10-day UAT vs 5-day deemed acceptance), define 'material defect' and severity levels, and issue written delivery notices to start the clock.

source.quote: Each deliverable will be deemed accepted if the Customer does not report a material defect in writing within five (5) business days of delivery.

risks.description: Three-way matching needs receipts, but the NetSuite integration scope lists only vendors, purchase orders, GL accounts and approved bills. Tolerance thresholds are not yet defined.
risks.recommendation: Confirm during discovery that item receipts will be synced from NetSuite and record that in the scope baseline. Capture tolerance thresholds in a signed discovery document.

source.quote: two-way and three-way matching of invoices to purchase orders and receipts

risks.description: Data migration of 'historical vendor data' has no record volume, no defined fields, no number of loads and no acceptance criteria. 'Historical' could be read to include inactive vendors or bank details. The boundary with excluded historical invoices may blur.
risks.recommendation: Agree at kickoff a record count limit, field list, number of migration loads and a reconciliation-based acceptance test, and confirm vendor bank details handling.

source.quote: Ledgerline will migrate the Customer's historical vendor data into the Platform.

risks.description: The three custom reports are 'specified by the Customer' with no due date for specifications and no complexity limit. Late or complex specs could push work past go-live.
risks.recommendation: Set a deadline for custom report specifications (e.g. end of discovery) and agree a complexity boundary using Platform reporting tools only, consistent with the custom development exclusion.

source.quote: up to three (3) custom reports specified by the Customer

risks.description: ACH and virtual card are enabled for 'US entities', but the contract does not say whether Harbor Warehousing LLC is a US entity. Payment rails per entity could be disputed.
risks.recommendation: Confirm the country and payment methods for each of the three entities at kickoff and record them in the project plan.

source.quote: Ledgerline will enable ACH and virtual card payments for US entities.

risks.description: SSO configuration requires Okta admin access, but no Customer obligation or date is listed. Section 4.1 sponsor and PM have no due date. Discovery and decisions may stall without them.
risks.recommendation: Request at kickoff a named Okta administrator with a date for access, and confirm the sponsor and PM by name before the first discovery workshop.

source.quote: The Customer will provide a project sponsor with decision-making authority and a day-to-day project manager.

risks.description: Only four 2-hour discovery workshops must cover intake, approval rules, matching tolerances and payments for three entities in two countries. That may be too little to finalize 15 workflows and thresholds.
risks.recommendation: Publish a workshop agenda at kickoff that allocates topics across the four sessions, and require pre-work from the Customer (current approval matrices, payment processes).

source.quote: up to four (4) discovery workshops of up to two hours each

risks.description: End-user training videos have no number, length or topic list. Hypercare does not define priority-1, whether 30 days are calendar or business days, or which time zone sets business hours.
risks.recommendation: Agree at kickoff a video list with topics and length, a priority definition matrix, and the hypercare calendar and time zone.

source.quote: provide recorded end-user training videos
